newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil steel consumption seen up 15 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil steel consumption seen up 15 pct in 1997.

text.p: Domestic steel consumption in Brazil is expected to rise 15 percent to a record 14.9 million tonnes this year compared with 13.0 million tonnes in 1996, the Brazilian Steel Institute said Tuesday.
The institute said in a statement higher consumption this year is due to improvement in the automobile, civil construction, capital goods and other industrial sectors that are heavy users of steel.
The prediction was made by the head of steelmaker Acesita, Wilson Brumer, who was named the institute's new president on Tuesday, the statement said.

Brumer based his figures on consumption of steel products in the first half of 1997, adding efforts to meet local demand will lower exports to 9.0 million tonnes this year from 9.74 million tonnes in 1996, it said.

He was quoted as saying the industry is now re-evaluating modernization projects, begun shortly after privatization of the sector, which called for $7.8 billion in investment in mills by the year 2000.
A new project would spend some $10 billion and raise installed capacity of Brazilian mills to 32 million tonnes a year from 28 million tonnes, he said.
